newsitem.title: UK: Rebel Lloyd's Names say they will seek better deal.
newsitem.headline: Rebel Lloyd's Names say they will seek better deal.

text.p: A group of dissatisfied backers of Lloyds of London will on Thursday hold a meeting to work out a strategy to try to win more compensation from the insurance market.

"Their aim is to bring to the attention of the community the enormity of what happened at Lloyd's," a spokesman for the group told Reuters on Wednesday, referring to record losses and allegations of negligence and mismanagement.
He added that the Names involved in the new group also hoped to obtain an improved offer of compensation for the 8.0 billion stg losses reported by Lloyd's in recent years.
The rebel Names are setting up a new group -- the United Names Organisation -- and will hold a news conference and meeting in London tomorrow, the spokesman said.
Most Names have accepted a 3.2 billion stg settlement offer from Lloyd's in partial compensation for their losses and agreed to end legal efforts to secure a better deal.
A spokesman for Lloyd's told Reuters that 32,294 Names had now accepted the offer -- including 119 late applicants -- out of a total of just over 34,000.
"There is no more money. There will be no further deal. Unless Names pay their debts, we'll be after them with writs," he added.
